conceptual assets.information: The enable setting activates the TWI controller, clears its FIFOs when disabled, and drives the external clock-generator enable. Controller operation depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes ctrl.enable at line 136, allowing an attacker to alter the controller's operating state. Availability is at risk because disabling ctrl.enable clears both FIFOs at line 168, resets clock generation at lines 252-254, and gates the external clock enable at line 270.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker writes the control register with enable cleared, disabling the TWI controller and discarding queued transfers.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and clock-divider settings determine the rate at which TWI transfers advance. TWI timing and continued transfer progress depend on these settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes modify ctrl.prsc and ctrl.cdiv at lines 137-138, which control the tick-generation path at lines 257-263. Availability is at risk because changing these values can suppress or excessively delay clk_gen.tick, preventing the engine from progressing at lines 328-344.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker writes an extreme prescaler or divider value to slow or stop TWI transfer progress.

conceptual assets.information: The queued command and acknowledge-control bits select the TWI operation performed by the engine, such as the protocol sequencing applied to a transfer. The command is decoded internally and has no direct output port carrying the command value itself.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus data is written into the transmit command word at line 198 and the command bits select engine.state at line 329, changing the operation performed. Availability is at risk because the selected command controls whether the engine enters and completes a TWI operation through the state machine at lines 328-344 and 385-394.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker queues a modified command word that causes an unintended TWI operation or leaves the requested transfer inactive.

conceptual assets.information: Payload data written by the bus is queued and serialized onto the TWI data line. A transfer depends on this payload remaining available and unmodified until transmission.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because bus-supplied payload can be sensitive and is exposed on twi_sda_o through the serial-data path at lines 374 and 406. Integrity is at risk because bus data enters the transmit FIFO at line 198 and is loaded into the engine shift path at line 327, where an attacker can replace the transmitted word. Availability is at risk because disabling the controller clears the transmit FIFO at line 168 and transmit consumption is gated by engine.busy, FIFO availability, and clk_gen.tick at line 199.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker observes the serial output or overwrites and clears queued transmit data before the intended TWI transfer occurs.

conceptual assets.information: Data sampled from the TWI data line is shifted into the receive path and returned to the bus through the receive FIFO. Software depends on the returned word representing the received transfer.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because received data can be sensitive and is exposed through the bus response data at line 156. Integrity is at risk because sampled twi_sda_i data is shifted into the receive word at lines 314 and 378 before being returned, so corruption of the sampled or stored value changes the reported word. Availability is at risk because disabling the controller clears the receive FIFO at line 168, preventing received data from being retained for a bus read.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker corrupts the sampled serial data or clears the receive buffer so software observes an altered or missing TWI word.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt request indicates that the controller is enabled, the transmit FIFO is empty, and the engine is not busy. System servicing of further TWI work can depend on this event.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because irq_o is produced from controller enable, FIFO availability, and engine busy state at line 239, so an attacker-induced status change can create a false interrupt. Availability is at risk because suppressing irq_o at line 239 can withhold the event used by the integrating system to service or continue TWI activity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker manipulates the controller or FIFO status conditions to generate spurious interrupts or suppress the interrupt needed for continued service.

considered, not kept.reason: clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset internal state and FIFO instances at lines 122, 127, 182-183, 213-214, and 303-312, so the clock/reset exclusion applies.
twi_scl_i and twi_scl_o are the serial link clock line and are excluded by the serial-clock rule, despite being sampled and driven at lines 407 and 409.
ctrl.clkstr is only read back at line 146 and used to shape the serial clock through clk_gen.halt at line 296, so the clock-shaping setting exclusion applies.
The bus request strobe, direction, and address only select register or FIFO accesses at lines 133-143 and 197-230, so Access command fields bars them as a separate concept.

The FIFO data paths and fill indicators only buffer, time, or report transfers between ports at lines 172-225 and 228-230, so Port buffers and Buffer and engine status bits bar them as separate concepts.

IO_TWI_FIFO and log2_fifo_size_c only fix FIFO construction and readback metadata at lines 20 and 64, so Build-time values bars them as run-time assets.
clkgen_i is used only as a condition allowing the internal counter and tick to advance at line 257, so Pacing pulses bars it as an independent concept.
